## Whistle Blower Policy and Guidelines
## General guidelines by Val
- Employees are required to work in an injury free manner displaying accepted levels of behaviour, avoid behaviours which jeopardize health, safety or security.
- Any conduct that places the employee or others at risk, or which threatens or intimidates others, is forbidden. These are considered serious misconduct and will normally result in disciplinary action, which may include immediate termination.
- Do not enter unauthorised areas.
- Maintenance or civil work should be carried out through required permit system.
- Employee should carry out their work according to Standard Operating Procedure.
- Employee while carrying operation should carry out each step to maintain safe & clean environment.
- Only undertake tasks for which you have been trained.
- Maintain all aisles, exits and vehicle traffic routes clear at all times.
- Maintain all exits unlocked at all times.
- Use and/or possession of illegal drugs or alcohol in company is forbidden.
- Smoking in company is forbidden.
- Use of Mobile phone within the company premises is banned.
## General responsibilities of Employee
- To read, understand and comply with Val’s Health, Safety and Environment policy, energy policy, water management policy, waste management policy, customer health & safety policy, safe work practices, safe job procedures and rules.
- As an employee of Val you have a legal duty to take reasonable care of yourself and others and to co-operate with the management on all aspects of health, safety & environment.
- Employee must not interfere with or misuse anything that's been provided for health or safety of employee.
- Employee must be aware of all emergency arrangements.
- Employee must report all incidents, near misses or damage to equipment and property.
- To intervene when witnessing unsafe acts or conditions.
- Employee must carry out your tasks in a safe manner following the Standard Operating Procedure.
- You have a duty to ensure that any personal protective equipment provided for your protection is worn, maintained and stored in the correct manner as directed.
## General Emergency Information
## Overview
Val Organics Pvt. Ltd has developed an Emergency Preparedness program so that we are ready for an unexpected disaster, whether it’s a natural or man-made one. Our first priority will always be life safety which includes evacuation & contingency plan.
## Preparation
Employees must attend training, become familiar with the Emergency Plan, and actively participate in emergency drills, treating them as if they are real.
## Chemical Emergencies
Always be ready for an emergency:
- Know the location of the nearest emergency and first aid equipment, including eye washes, emergency showers, fire alarms and fire extinguishers.
- Be aware of those employees in your workplace or nearby who have special emergency training or skills.
- Know the nearest paging call stations and the paging call station number - #777 for help.
- Be able to tell emergency personnel the exact name of the chemical involved.
## Unconsciousness
Call #777 through paging call station for help or press the manual call point. Before entering an area to help an unconscious person, make sure that you will not be in danger from hazardous fumes or inadequate oxygen. Respirators and lifelines may be needed but should only be used by individuals previously trained. If you are able to enter the area remove the victim to fresh air immediately. Provide adequate first aid by first aider while waiting for medical personnel. If the victim’s eyes or skin are contaminated, flush with running water. Remove any contaminated clothing.
## Fumes
If you work with chemicals, be aware of warning symptoms of overexposure to hazardous fumes. Get fresh air immediately if you sense a burning of irritation in your nose, throat, or lungs; have difficulty breathing; feel weak, dizzy or nauseous; or notice a strong odour. Close the source if possible. If these measures don’t help, leave the area & checking all the person are evacuated & plant is in safe mode.
## Eye Contact
Flush your eye immediately with running water. Use an emergency shower or eye wash station. Hold your eyelids apart and roll your eyeballs. Do not use ointments or salves, which may be dangerous. Continue flushing for at least 15 minutes. Get immediate medical attention.
## Skin Contact
Drench your clothing and skin thoroughly with plenty of water. Use emergency shower. Remove contaminated clothing while drenching it and continue to flush skin with water for at least 15 minutes. Get medical attention.
## Evacuation Emergencies
If you hear the alarm or discover an emergency such as a fire, explosion, gas leak, chemical spill, or a violent situation:
- Remain calm
- Press the nearest manual call point
- If possible, declare the severity & type of incident on paging call station.

chapters.title: Environment
chapters.text:
It is critical to protect the environment so as to reduce the destruction of eco-systems. It is more of a moral obligation for humans to protect the environment from pollution and other activities that lead to environmental degradation. Importantly, environmental degradation is detrimental since it threatens the long-term health of the animals, humans and plants.
It is everyone’s responsibility to take care of the environment to make this planet a wonderful place to live.
## Energy Consumption
## Overview
Reducing energy consumption limits the number of carbon emissions in the environment which play a significant role in climate change. Reduced emissions result in cleaner air quality & help sustain the resources we already have.
## nspections
Workplace inspections are carried out through Internal Audit for the reduction in energy consumption & finding solutions for energy reduction.
## Employee Responsibilities
- HSE head is responsible for introducing and maintaining cost-effective ways of providing management information about energy consumption.
- HSE head is responsible to provide training to employees through which we can save or reduce the consumption of energy.
- HSE head is responsible for raising and maintaining energy awareness throughout organisation.
- All employees working in plant are responsible to report the source of energy wastage.
- All employees working in plant are free to provide any suggestion or techniques reducing energy consumption.
- Employee performing the job must follow the correct procedures in accordance with the VOPL/HSE/010: SOP of Waste Management.
## Water Consumption
## Overview
Reducing water consumption usages reduces the energy required to process and deliver & energy required to treat the waste water which in turn, helps to reduce pollution and conserve fuel resources.
## nspections
Workplace inspections are carried out through Internal Audit for the reduction in water consumption & finding solutions for reduction in water consumption.
## Employee Responsibilities
- HSE head is responsible in introducing and maintaining cost-effective ways of providing management information about water consumption.
- HSE head is responsible to provide training to employees through which we can save or reduce the consumption of water.
- HSE head is responsible for raising and maintaining water awareness throughout organisation.
- All employees working in plant are free to report the source of water wastage.
- All employees working in plant are free to provide any suggestion or techniques reducing water consumption.
## Local Pollution
## Overview
Air pollution, water pollution, soil pollution & noise pollution are the impacts from company operations on local environment around company facilities through the emissions of dust, noise, odour, accidental pollution and road congestion.
## nspections
Report & Workplace inspections are carried out through Internal Audit for the management & monitoring of environment pollution.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Factory Manager, HSE Head & Plant Incharge are responsible for ensuring their company’s compliance with the procedure.
- Area Incharge/ HSE Head is responsible for providing training.
- Employee performing the job must follow the correct procedures in accordance with the VOPL/HSE/030: SOP of Management & Monitoring of Environmental Pollution.
- HSE Personnel is responsible for the monitoring of pollution.
- Quality Control department personnel are responsible for the analysis of effluent water.
- Maintenance head is responsible for the preventive maintenance of pollution control equipment.
## Labelling, Handling & Storing of Chemicals and Waste
## Overview
Raw materials, chemicals, non-hazardous and hazardous waste generated from operations is necessary as when improperly labelled, handled or stored, can cause substantial harm to human health, safety or to the environment.
## nspections
Workplace inspections are carried out through Internal Audit for the labelling, Handling & Storage of Chemical & Waste.
## Employee Responsibilities
- HSE Head & Area Incharge are responsible for ensuring their company’s compliance with this procedure.
- Area Incharge/ HSE Head is responsible for providing training.
- Employee performing the job must follow the correct procedures in accordance with the VOPL/HSE/027: SOP of Labelling, Handling & Storing of Hazardous Materials.
## Waste Management
## Overview
## Waste management is very necessary in the present day context for the following reasons: To prevent pollution of the environment and its natural resources like air, water and land; To prevent complete exhaustion of the resources like minerals, water, etc.; To produce energy which could be an alternative for the fast depleting fossil fuels and other conventional sources of energy; To make optimum use of the waste generated; For a better and sustainable future.

chapters.title: First Aid
chapters.text:
## Overview
First aid is the care given to an injured worker before professional medical help arrives. First aid may mean the difference between life and death. The purpose of this section is to preserve life, prevent any injuries from getting worse, and to help injured worker recover.
## nspections
First Aid box & other medical things related to first aid are checked through the inspections carried out in Internal Audit.
## Employee Responsibilities
- HSE Head/Factory appointed Doctor is responsible to provide training to first aider of plant.
- First Aider of particular area is responsible to maintain first aid box fully stocked.
- First Aider is responsible to first aid the injured person.
- First Aider is responsible to log the first aid case with the injury/disease description & description of First Aid provided.
## Pre-Medical Check Up
## Overview
Pre-employment check-ups are a means to establish baseline health data against which the future health status of the employee can be compared. It is also a means of identifying existing medical conditions, which can help to protect the employee if there is any risk associated with the occupational exposure.
## nspections
Records of Pre-medical check-up of new joining are checked through the inspections carried out in Internal Audit.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Human resource Head is responsible to carry out pre-medical check-up of new joining.
- Human resource head is responsible to check whether the employee is fit or unfit according to the medical report & will take the action according to VOPL/HR/007: SOP of Pre-medical check-up.
## Regular Medical Check Up
## Overview
Regular medical check-up helps your employee to keep a track on their health status and thus take precautionary steps at the right time.
## nspections
Records of Regular medical check-up of all employees are checked through the inspections carried out in Internal Audit.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Human resource Head is responsible to schedule regular medical check-up of employee after every six month.
- Factory appointed doctor is responsible to visit the site every Saturday.
- All the employees are responsible for their half yearly medical check-up.
- Any employee can discuss their health related issue to factory doctor on his visit on Saturday.
## Customer Health and Safety
## Overview
We ensure our customers health & safety by keeping our global supply chain intact safer by ensuring all HSEQ standards maintained at its most at our site.
## nspections
The systems in the organization can be continuously assessed, monitored & improve with the help of Internal Audit.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Factory Manager is responsible for sharing major changes to customers as mentioned in the VOPL/QA/019: SOP of Customer Health & Safety.
- All employees are responsible to follow VOPL/QA/019: SOP of Customer Health & Safety for standard, safer processing techniques and practices which ensure continuous supply and quality products.
## Reporting Hazards
## Overview
A hazard is something that has the potential to cause harm, ill health or injury during the course of the work activity.
## Employee Responsibilities
- It is the duty of all employees to report hazards to their HSE head immediately.
- HSE head is responsible to assess the situation and introduce the necessary control measures, so far as is reasonably practicable, to prevent injury or unsafe conditions.
- It is the duty of head of particular department to whom the responsibility is given by HSE head to introduce necessary control measures.
## Workplace Inspections
## Overview
Workplace inspections are the primary mechanism for recognition, assessment, and control of hazards in the workplace. By working together, we can manage workplace hazards and support a healthy and safe work environment.
## nspections
Workplace inspections is carried out through Internal Audit.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Employee must cooperate with any inspections and let the HSE personnel know of any hazards you are aware of.
- Supervisor is responsible to identify and control hazards, as part of their regular duties.
Safety of employees refers to the provision of a safe working environment, safe equipment, policies, and procedures in order to ensure worker’s safety.
Safety in the workplace has a significant impact in business KPIs. In other words, safer working environments benefit from fewer accidents, which results in fewer occupational health costs, better employee retention and satisfaction, less employee downtime, and less retraining time.
## Work Place Hazards
## Ergonomics
## Overview
Injuries of the muscles, nerves, tendons, ligaments, joints, cartilage, spinal discs, blood vessels or related soft tissue including a sprain, strain and inflammation. Ergonomics hazards occur when the job, or the way it is done, does not fit the worker's physical capabilities, and the worker uses their body to adjust to difficult or awkward situations.

chapters.title: Working Hours
chapters.text:
## Overview
The normal work week in Val Organics Pvt. Ltd. consist of six (6) days & eight (8) hours for shift personnel and eight & half (8.5) hours for general shift personnel & will vary with employee based on their week off. Work hours are different for different shifts. Four shifts are run in Val. Work hours for First shift is 7:00 to 15:00, Second shift is 15:00 to 23:00, Night shift is 23:00 to 7:00 & General shift is 10:00 to 18:30, including half hour for lunch. All the management personnel will work in general shift. Head of employee will allocate the shift to employee that best suits the need of the work through shift schedule for the month.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Helpers, Operators & Supervisor is responsible to report for any kind working conditions i.e. wages, overtime, or working hours to their respective head i.e. Plant Head.
- Plant Head is responsible to report for any working conditions i.e. wages, overtime, or working hours to their head i.e. Factory Manager.
- Factory Manager is responsible to report for any kind of working conditions i.e. wages, overtime, or working hours to their head i.e. Factory Director.

chapters.title: Wages
chapters.text:
## Overview
The Val’s wages guidelines are designed to provide you with a salary that is competitive with local and national market conditions. All positions are classified under specific titles and salary grades or ranges. Wages increases occur within minimum to maximum ranges assigned to each job classification.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Management personnel are responsible to decide the appropriate wages to the employees.
- Human Resource head is responsible to input accurate information of wages into the computerized business system.
## Extra hours working benefits
## Overview
When operating requirements or other needs cannot be met during regular working hours, Employees may be scheduled to work overtime. When possible, advance notification of these assignments will be provided. All overtime work must be authorized in advance by their head. The Company will attempt to distribute overtime evenly. The Company provides compensation for all overtime hours worked by employees in accordance with his/her salary. Overtime will be paid for 1.5 times the regular hourly rate for hours worked beyond the standard 40-hour workweek. Employees will be expected to work the hours documented in their offer letter at time of hire. Any hours worked in excess without their heads approval may result in disciplinary action.
## Employee Responsibility
Human resource head is responsible to provide extra hours working benefits to employee.
## Salary Administration
## Overview
Salary is distributed in all employees account in between date 5 & 7, except when either of those days falls on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday, in which case salary will be distributed on the preceding workday. All salary deductions are itemized and presented to employees with the salary slip. Approved salary deductions will include: professional taxes & provident fund.
## Employee Responsibility
Human Resource head is responsible for the administration of salary.
## Worker’s Compensation
## Overview
If employee suffers a work-related injury or illness while working in the company, Val provides employees benefits to replace lost income and to compensate for certain permanent losses to the body. Compensation benefits include a return-to-work program to help employees resume productive activity. It is important to report a work-related injury as soon as possible. Human Resource department will help you with this process. Other than this Val offer compensation for the following components.
- Compensation Components
- The remuneration package consists of the following elements:
- Base Salary: A fixed regular pay rate corresponding to the assigned job classification.
- Shift Differentials: Supplementary pay premiums for working specific shifts, such as nights or weekends.
- Performance-Based Pay: Implementation of incentive programs to reward surpassing performance targets, such as productivity bonuses or safety incentives.
- Overtime Pay: Compensation for employees exceeding their scheduled hours at an overtime rate, as dictated by relevant laws and regulations.
- Benefits: Provision of a comprehensive benefits package, encompassing health insurance, paid time off (PTO), and retirement plans (specifics detailed in a separate benefits manual).

## Employee Responsibilities
- Employee is responsible to report work related injury while working in company as soon as possible.
- Human Resource head is responsible for the worker’s compensation injured while working in the company.
- Human Resource head is responsible for the worker’s compensation according to compensation components.
## Probationary Period
## Overview
Employees serve a probationary period of six month from their employment date. This is a trial period during which the management learn whether the employee is suited for the job. This time may be extended if the employee is not compatible to handle the situation.

chapters.title: Employee Conduct
chapters.text:
## Standards of Conduct
## Overview
To ensure orderly operations and provide the best possible work environment, VAL expects Employees to follow rules of conduct that will protect the interests and safety of all Team Members and the organization. The purpose of these rules is not to restrict your rights, but rather to be certain that you understand what conduct is expected and necessary. While it is not possible to list all the forms of behaviour that are considered unacceptable in the workplace, the following are examples of infractions of rules of conduct that may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment. This list is illustrative only; types of conduct that threaten security, personal safety, employee welfare and Company operations are also prohibited.
- Violation of any policy, practice and/or procedure.
- Neglect of job responsibilities or unsatisfactory performance.
- Falsification, misrepresentation or alteration of employment records, employment information, or other Company records, including lying about sick or personal leave; falsifying reason for a leave of absence or other data requested by the Company.
- Theft and deliberate or careless damage or destruction of any Company property, or the property of any employee, customer, supplier, or visitor in any manner.
- Theft or unauthorized removal or borrowing of Company property or the property of fellow employees without prior authorization, including unauthorized use of Company equipment, time, materials, or facilities;
- Engaging in acts of violence, making threats of violence toward anyone, intimidating, fighting, or provoking a fight during working hours, or on Company property, or when representing the Company.
- Engaging in criminal conduct whether or not related to job performance;
- Insubordination, including but NOT limited to failure or refusal to obey the lawful orders or instructions of a supervisor, member of management of Val, or the use of abusive or threatening language toward a supervisor or member of management of Val.
- Using inappropriate language such as: profanity, cussing, swearing, vulgar, obscene, abusive or insulting language, including unwelcome name calling and inappropriate jokes or racial slurs at any time on Company premises.
- Displaying indifference or rudeness towards a customer or fellow employee; or any disorderly/antagonistic conduct on company premises.
- Immoral conduct or indecency on Company property.
- Conducting a lottery or gambling on Company premises.
- Failing to obtain permission to leave work for any reason during normal working hours.
- Sleeping or loitering on scheduled work time.
- Violating any safety, health, security or Company policy, rule, or procedure.
- Committing a fraudulent act or breach of trust under any circumstances.
- Any act of harassment, sexual, racial or other; telling racist jokes; making racial or ethnic slurs.
- Being under the influence of illegal drugs while at work; use, possession or sale of illegal drug in any quantity while on company premises.
- Solicitations or distribution of any nature on Val property during scheduled work time.
- Violating safety rules, practices, or engaging in conduct that creates a health & safety hazard, including smoking. Please note: nothing in this list alters the Company’s policy of at-will employment.
- The Company remains free to terminate the employment relationship at any time, with or without notice, and in the absence of any violation of these rules.
## Attendance & Punctuality
## Overview
Attendance is a key factor in your job performance. Punctuality and regular attendance are expected from employees. Excessive absences (whether excused or unexcused) or leaving early is unacceptable. When reporting an absence, you should indicate the nature of the problem causing your absence and your expected return to work date. A physician’s statement may be required as proof of the need for any illness‐related absence regardless of the length of the absence. Except as provided in other policies, an employee who is absent from work for three consecutive days without notification to his or her head will be considered to have voluntarily terminated his or her employment. Excessive absences, tardiness or leaving early will be grounds for discipline up to and including termination.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Employee is responsible to report in case of absent for any reason or plan to arrive late or leave early to his/her respective head.
- Employee is responsible to report in the event of an emergency leave.
- For leave on any occasion employee is responsible to take permission of his/her respective head & factory manager mentioning particular duration leave on leave application.
- Employee is responsible to approve leave application two weeks prior to leave.
- Employee is responsible to submit the leave application approved by his/her respective head & factory manager to Human Resource head.

chapters.title: Dress Code
chapters.text:
## Overview
Each Employee is a representative of the Company in the eyes of the public, so employee should always report to work properly groomed and wearing uniform provided by VAL. VAL provides 2 pairs of uniform to every employee each year which help us to fulfil varying goals of comfort, professionalism, safety and image. VAL Employee is expected to wear provided uniform neatly and in a manner consistent with the nature of business and the type of work performed. Employees who report to work inappropriately dressed may be asked to leave the workplace until they are properly dressed or groomed. Under such circumstance, you will be asked to clock out and return in acceptable attire. Consult your supervisor if you have questions as to what constitutes appropriate appearance. Where necessary, reasonable accommodation may be made to a person with a disability. Employees who violate dress code standards may be subject to appropriate disciplinary action.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Employee is responsible for reporting to work with appropriate clothing.
- Human Resource head is responsible to ask the employee to leave who report to work inappropriately dressed.
## Labour Relations
## Overview
Labour relations are the term used to define the process between employers and employees or management and unions in order to make decisions in organizations.
There are no unions as the employees are satisfied with the way Val’s management treats employees with good relationship.
There is no employee representative & every employee is free to share their concern directly to management.
Workers participation in management is encouraged indicating involvement of workers in managerial decision making process of the organization.
Strategies of Val for better relationship between management & employee.
- Fair and consistent policies and practices.
- Open door management policies.
- Competitive pay and benefits.
- Employee satisfaction survey.
- Employee trust and recognition.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Management personnel are responsible to listen to the concern raised by employee & find solution for it.
- Management personnel are responsible to maintain fair & consistent policies and practices.
- Human Resource head is responsible to carry out employee satisfaction survey.

chapters.title: Child and Forced Labour
chapters.text:
## Overview
Child labour is work carried out from children less than 18 years that harms them or exploits them in some way - physically, mentally, morally, or by blocking their access to education. Val has implemented control mechanisms at the level of hiring procedures to prevent child labour. It is necessary to verify the age of applicants for employment by requiring presentation of Valid identification issued by an official authority prior to employment. A copy of such identification and all other legally required documentation must be kept on file during the entire procedure of employment.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Human resource head is responsible for verification of the authenticity of documents submitted at the time of recruitment.
- Human Resource head is responsible to maintain all legal documents in the employee file during the process of recruitment.
- For any complaints, concerns and queries regarding child labour any employee or stakeholder is responsible to contact to Human resource Head on (hr@valorganics.com/ Mob. No.- 9274099615) or in the absence of Human resource Head to Factory Manager on (hasmukh.prajapati@valorganics.com / Mob. No.-9377009858) according to VOPL/HR/011: SOP of Child & Forced Labour Prevention.
- Human resource Head is responsible for implementing remedial plan for the child labour according to VOPL/HR/011: SOP of Child & Forced Labour Prevention.
## Overview
Forced labour is work that is performed involuntarily and under the menace of any penalty. Val will not tolerate any form of forced labour. Acceptance of the Val Standards, which condemn and prohibit all forms of the forced labour, is a basic prerequisite.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Human Resource head is responsible to provide annual training on Forced Labour.
- Employee is responsible to recognize and report violations by forced labour to Human Resource head.
- For any complaints, concerns and queries regarding forced labour any employee or stakeholder is responsible to contact to Human resource Head on (hr@valorganics.com/ Mob. No.- 9274099615) or in the absence of Human resource Head to Factory Manager on (hasmukh.prajapati@valorganics.com / Mob. No.- 9377009858) according to VOPL/HR/011: SOP of Child & Forced Labour Prevention.
- Human resource Head is responsible for implementing remedial plan for the forced labour according to VOPL/HR/011: SOP of Child & Forced Labour Prevention.
## Career Management
Career Management is a life-long process of investing resources to accomplish your future career goals. It is a continuing process that allows you to adapt to the changing demands of our dynamic economy. The career management process embraces various concepts: Management of recruitments, training, Self-awareness, career development planning/career exploration.
## Management of recruitments
## Overview
Val Organics Pvt. Ltd. believes that hiring qualified individuals to fill positions contributes to the overall success of the company. Each employee is hired to make significant contributions to Val. VAL is doing blind screening of resumes to ensure unbiased evaluation of candidates qualifications and skills. VAL provide regular diversity and inclusion training for hiring managers and decision-makers.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Department head is responsible for the requisitions of new employee for recruitment to factory manager.
- Factory Manager is responsible for the approval and then department head will forward it to the human resource department.
- HR will arrange a meeting with the factory manager prior to posting a job opening to learn more about the position, the requirements and the profile of the ideal candidate.
- HR is responsible to create job postings that briefly describe the job opening as per the VOPL/HR/001: SOP of Employee Recruitment.
- The HR department and the factory manager is responsible to screen resumes prior to scheduling interviews.
- Factory Manager is responsible to conduct interviews using behaviour and technical based interview questions
- Factory manager is responsible to give the list of recruited candidates to HR.
- HR department is responsible to discuss the salary structure to the recruited candidates.
- Human Resource personnel is responsible to provide final job offer letter to recruited personnel ready to join, once HR department receives satisfactory results from all required background & pre-medical check-up.
## A. Forced and child labour
Suppliers shall prohibit use of child labour at any stage of their business process. We expect that our suppliers will not employ any person below the age of 18 (or as per local law, whichever is greater). The suppliers must not use forced labour including prison or debt bondage labour, human trafficking or modern day slavery.

chapters.title: Training
chapters.text:
## Overview
Finding skilled employees is becoming difficult in this digital age. Employees are the backbone of your organization and investing in their skills is not only beneficial for them but also for the organization's growth.
To help employees become familiar with the Company and the way of their doing things, the Val will provide different training session within the first few days after employee begin work. The sequence for training will be: Training in the start will be through Human Resource department followed by Health, Safety & Environment department and lastly by process department. In addition, the Company will periodically offer additional training or educational program.
## Employee Responsibilities
- HR head will be responsible to provide training regarding the policies, rules & regulations, code of conduct of the company to the recruited personnel.
- HSE head will be responsible to provide training regarding the policies & topics including Health, Safety & Environment of the company to the recruited personnel.
- Area Head will be responsible to provide training regarding the process, troubleshooting, Do’s & Don’ts
- All HR head, HSE head & Area head will arrange periodical training for employees based on requirements.
- Heads of different department should work with employees and managers to set new goals for training.
- An employee must be provided with the training roadmap. It helps them to get an idea about the importance of training and encourages involvement.
- Employee is responsible to attain all type of periodic training.

chapters.title: Career development
chapters.text:
## Overview
Career development has become primary activity of organizations in order to create a pool of talented employees as well as enhance their career satisfaction. Along with this, it is also considered as an organized and planned process to improve the efficiency of organization. Employees have their own personal desires and aspirations and need to effectively utilize their personal skills to attain their career goals and objectives. On the other hand, organizations have needs for staffing and meeting present and future human resource requirements. A career development system is a mechanism that takes both the parties in to consideration and helps them meet their requirements as well as objectives.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Employees must take individual responsibility for their careers by maintaining their individual talent profiles, focusing on personal development, demonstrating company Values, and building their professional networks.
- Respective departmental heads are responsible for providing career coaching and candid performance feedback to employees, identifying opportunities for development, and advising employees about potential job opportunities.
- Respective departmental heads should actively support employees in setting clear goals and personal objectives, assessing potential, identifying career options, and providing growth opportunities through assignments, developmental programmes, exposure, and visibility to other parts of the organisation and leaders.
- HR’s role is to provide the tools and resources for employees to manage their careers and for respective departmental heads to help employees in going so, aligned with organisational and business needs.
## Career mobility
## Overview
Career mobility is a practice of moving people within an organization, in hopes that new skills will be gained and sharpened through the employee’s new roles and responsibilities. The objective is to have the right talent at the right place at the right time to ensure business results and successful business outcomes. It means that with a career mobility program, you have an idea to get your employees from their current job role to a better job role where they are be of more Value to your organization.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Human Resource & Plant Head is responsible to think of a talent mobility program as the idea of moving talent in organization to a lateral in-house position where they can better leverage their competencies, experience and skills towards organizational goals.
- Employee is responsible to talk to his respective head for his/her career mobility if the employee think his competencies, experience and skills will prove more worthy in different career.
- For career mobility all employee has to follow accordingly to VOPL/HR/014: SOP of Career Management.
## Harassment, Discrimination & Equal Opportunity
## Overview
Val is committed to providing equal employment opportunity for all employees and job applicants regardless of their race, colour, religion, sex, age, national origin, disability, and political affiliation. Employment discrimination based upon these traits is unlawful under both state and central law. Equal opportunity extends to all aspects of employment including hiring, transfers, promotions, training, termination, working conditions, compensation, benefits, and other terms and conditions of employment. The Val complies with central and state equal employment opportunity laws and strives to keep the workplace free from all forms of unlawful discrimination, including harassment and retaliation.
Harassment: Harassment is any form of behaviour that is unwelcomed, unsolicited, unreciprocated and usually (but not always) repeated. It is behaviour that is likely to offend, humiliate, or intimidate. It can make it difficult for effective work to be done by the employee or affected by this behaviour. For harassment to occur there does not have to be an intention to offend or harass. It is the impact of the behaviour on the person who is receiving it, together with the nature of the behaviour, which determines whether it is harassment.
Discrimination: Discrimination refers to treating a person or a group of people less favourably than another person or group such as sex, age, race or disability.
Equal Opportunity: To provide opportunities regardless of race, age, religion, disability, colour, marital status, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, genetic conditions or predispositions, or certain military and veteran status.
## Employee Responsibilities
- All employees are responsible to follow the standards of behaviour outlined in the policy.
- All employees are responsible to treat everyone with dignity, courtesy and respect.
- All employees of Val are responsible for maintaining and promoting an environment which is free of harassment and discrimination and for promptly reporting any incidents which they believe to be acts of discrimination or harassment.

chapters.title: Diversity, Equity & Inclusion
chapters.text:
## Overview
Diversity, equity and inclusion are three interconnected concepts that work together to promote healthy communities and places of work free of stereotyping and mistreatment.
Diversity: Diversity involves all the ways that people are different, including the various characteristics that distinguish one demographic or individual from another. Elements of diversity include race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic status, gender identity, religion, language, age, marital status, veteran status, mental ability, physical abilities and disabilities. Diversity also includes the range of ideas, perspectives and values people have. VAL acknowledges that people aren't sets of specific characteristics and that each voice is unique. Real diversity requires a deeper understanding of each person as an individual rather than a stereotype. VAL welcomes different perspectives and backgrounds to a business and actively seeking them out.
Equity: Equity aims to ensure equal treatment, access, opportunity and advancement for people, including employees in the workplace. Equity attempts to identify and remove barriers that prevent some people/groups from fully participating in certain jobs and industries. The aim of equity is to promote justice, fairness and impartiality. VAL adopt equity practices and don't establish one size fits all policies. Instead, VAL take individual needs into consideration, while also readjusting organizational structures to account for the disadvantages and inequities.
Inclusion: Inclusion builds a culture where everyone feels welcome. It actively invites every person and group to contribute and participate. An inclusive, welcoming environment supports and embraces differences. A work environment that's inclusive is supportive, respectful and collaborative, and encourages all employees to participate and contribute. VAL gives each worker room to flourish and succeed in a work environment. VAL gives all employees the opportunity to voice their opinions and ensuring they aren't excluded based on their identities. It's also about enabling employees to see themselves reflected in their organization’s values.
## Affinity groups for minorities/vulnerable groups
## Overview
An affinity group is a self-organized group of employees with a shared identity or interest. These groups seek to support and amplify the priorities and concerns of systemically non-dominant peoples. Val prefers creating affinity groups for minorities/vulnerable groups to reduce negative impacts of dominant identity culture. By creating affinity groups for minorities/vulnerable groups in workplace Val creates safe spaces for networking, resources for mentorship and training for professional development. Affinity groups have recognized benefits for both VAL and the employees, including:
- Attracting, recruiting, and retaining employees.
- Promoting diversity, cultural awareness, and an inclusive work environment.
- Increasing employee job satisfaction, morale, and productivity.
- Fostering professional development and learning through mentoring, networking, open dialogue, and the exchange of ideas.
- Providing a support group for employees.
- Enhancing the employer’s public image in its marketing, recruiting, business development, and other external efforts.
## Who may join an Affinity Group?
All VAL employees are encouraged to join an Affinity Group with fellow employees they share an identity with. Specifically:
- Affinity group members must be employed by VAL.
- Any VAL Employee may apply to start an affinity group during the open application period.
- The formation of the Affinity Group must rely on volunteers and efforts must stem from a grassroots nature.
- Neither VAL nor members of the group may pressure any employee into joining or participating.
- Membership and participation in an Affinity Group shall be entirely voluntary
## Women's development programs
## Overview
Women development programs refers to the creation of programs for women where they can make decisions of their own for their personal benefits as well as for the society. VAL has taken significant steps to empower women, creating opportunities to achieve economic independence and enhance their quality of life. VAL is empowering woman by women's development, mentorship, and sponsorship programs.
Following are some of women's development, mentorship, and sponsorship programs:
- Women-focused leadership development initiatives are implemented to empower and advance female employees in their careers.
- Mentorship programs pair female employees with experienced mentors to provide guidance and support in their professional growth.
- Training workshops and seminars specifically tailored to address the needs and challenges faced by women in the workplace are conducted regularly.
- Networking events are organized to connect female employees with industry professionals and create opportunities for career advancement.

chapters.title: Performance Evaluations
chapters.text:
## Overview
Val conducts periodic performance reviews/evaluations annually in March. The goal of a performance review is to identify areas where an employee excels and areas that need improvement.
All performance reviews are based on merit, achievement and other factors may include but are not limited to:
- Quality of work
- Attitude
- Knowledge of work
- Job skills
- Attendance and punctuality
- Teamwork and cooperation
- Compliance with company policy
- Past performance reviews
- Improvement
- Acceptance of responsibility and constructive feedback
The performance evaluations are intended for the increments or promotions of employee i.e. better the performance evaluation/review, better the increment.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Factory manager is responsible to perform evaluations on scheduled review date.
- Respective Area/Plant head is responsible for employee performance evaluations which will review accordingly to VOPL/HR/014: SOP of Career Management.
## Promotions
## Overview
Employee maybe promoted from his current job based on performance evaluation match him with the job for which he/she is suited and/or to meet the business and operational needs of the Company.
Reasons for promotion may include, but are not necessarily limited to, fluctuations in department workloads or production flow; a desire for more efficient utilization of personnel; increased career opportunities; personal conflicts; health; other personal situations; or other business reasons.
The management of the Company does reserve the right, however, to transfer or promote an employee without posting the availability of that position.
VAL have established clear promotion criteria based solely on merit and performance, mitigating any biases. Encourage diverse representation on promotion committees to ensure fair decision-making. Conduct regular audits of promotion and development processes to identify and address any disparities or discriminatory practices.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Employee is responsible to request a promotion after completion of 2 years of satisfactory performance in your current job.
- Management personnel are responsible to promote the employee based on needed skills, education, experience and other qualifications for the job.
## WORKPLACE ETIQUETTE
## Return of property
## Overview
All Company property, assigned to Employees including desks, computers, vehicles, work areas and equipment are to be used and maintained according to Company rules and regulations. They should be kept clean and used only for work-related purposes. No personal locks may be used on Company provided lockers unless the Employee furnishes a copy of the key or the combination to the lock to a Human Resources Department. Unauthorized use of a personal lock by an Employee may result in losing the right to use a Company locker.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Human Resource department is responsible to inspect all Company property to ensure compliance with its rules and regulations, at any time and without notice to the Employee, not necessarily in the Employee’s presence.
- Employee is responsible to reasonably protect and safeguard company’s property from loss and damage.
- Employee is responsible for the repair or replacement cost of company’s property.
- Employee is responsible to return company’s property at the time of his/her termination.
- HR department is responsible to deduct cash from pay check if the Value of any property issued is not returned.
## Nondisclosure of confidential information
## Overview
Any information that an employee learns about Val Organics Pvt. Ltd, as a result of working for Val Organics Pvt. Ltd. that is not publicly available constitutes confidential information. Employees may not disclose confidential information to anyone who is not employed by Val or to other persons employed by Val who do not need to know such information. The protection of privileged and confidential information, including trade secrets, manufacturing details is vital to the interests and the success of Val. The disclosure, distribution, electronic transmission or copying of Val’s confidential information is prohibited.
Employees are required to sign a non‐disclosure agreement as a condition of employment. Any employee who discloses confidential Val information will be subject to disciplinary action. Discussions involving sensitive information should always be held in confidential settings to safeguard the confidentiality of the information
## Employee Responsibilities
- Every employee is responsible not to disclose confidential information to anyone who is not employed by Val or to other persons employed by Val who do not need to know such information.
- Every employee is responsible to avoid Conversations regarding confidential information generally on cellular phones, or in elevators, restrooms, restaurants, or other places where conversations might be overheard.

chapters.title: Conflict of Interest
chapters.text:
## Overview
Employees are required to avoid ethical, legal, financial, or other conflicts of interest and to ensure that their activities and interests do not conflict with their obligations to the Val. Use of Company funds, property, or time for improper purposes and other deceptive and/or dishonest practices is absolutely forbidden. The best interest of the Company must be each employee’s priority without actions indicating divided loyalty and/or self-dealing.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Employee is responsible to maintain a high standard of conduct and refrain from exerting influence in any transaction where an employee’s interests may conflict with the best interests of the Company or where the employee may gain any financial benefit.
- An employee who encounters a personal interest that may have the potential of conflicting with the interests of the Val is responsible to discuss immediately to human resource department.
- Employee is responsible to report promptly to management any remuneration received from an individual or concern with which the Company does business.
- Employee is responsible to refrain from lending money to, borrowing money from, or having loans guaranteed by anyone doing business with the Company.
- Employee is responsible to refrain from using information or knowledge acquired by virtue of their position in the Company for any personal gain or advantage, by divulging such knowledge or information to anyone who would use it in any manner detrimental to the interest of the Company.
- Employee is responsible to accept no employment or compensation or engage in any business or professional activity that might require disclosure of the Company’s confidential information.
- Employee is responsible to not to work with an outside professional organization or association.
- Employee is responsible to report to the Company any knowledge of the existence of a violation of the above policy to Human Resource Department.
- Human Resource department is responsible to take disciplinary action on the employee whose interest/activity conflict with the interest of Val.
- Human Resource department is responsible for ensuring that this Interest of conflict is communicated to and understood by the employees and that it is effectively enforced.
## Fraud
## Overview
Fraud is any illegal acts characterized by deceit, concealment, or violation of trust. These acts are not dependent upon the application or threat of violence or of physical force. Fraud is perpetrated by parties and organizations to obtain money, property, or services; to avoid payment or loss of services; or to secure personal or business advantage.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Employee is responsible to act at all times with the highest degree of honesty, integrity, accountability, and propriety.
- Employee is responsible conduct their duties in a manner the does not jeopardize, to the contrary, safeguards the Company’s resources and assets.
- Human Resource head is responsible to monitor business activities of employees and be aware of and alert to potential signs of fraud.
- For any complaints, concerns and queries regarding fraud any employee or stakeholder is responsible to contact to ethics officer on (akshay.chadha@valorganics.com/ Mob. No.- 9987425522) or in the absence of ethics officer to Human resource Head on (hr@valorganics.com/ Mob. No.- 9274099615) according to VOPL/HR/013: SOP of Anti-Corruption & Bribery, Anti-Fraud and Anti-Money laundering.
- Ethics Officer and Human Resource Head is responsible to investigate incidents on fraud according to VOPL/HR/013: SOP of Anti-Corruption & Bribery, Anti-Fraud and Anti-Money laundering.
## Money laundering
## Overview
Money laundering is the process of changing large amounts of money obtained from crimes into origination from a legitimate source. At Val, we do not allow dirty money to play any part in our business. But while it is easy to state that as a fundamental principle, protecting our company against attempts by criminals to "clean" cash and other assets generated by illegal activities is a challenge that demands constant vigilance, from us all. Because being involved in money-laundering or terrorism financing – even inadvertently – is a criminal offence.
## Employee Responsibilities
- Management personnel are responsible to do business only with reputable partners who operate within the law, using resources from legitimate sources.
- Management personnel are responsible to check the identity and credentials of potential customers, business partners and other third parties.
- Management personnel are responsible to take all reasonable measures to ensure transparent business relationships.
